title: The Shattered Vaunt
subtitle: When the Vaunting Breaks, the World Trembles

listing.blurb: When the Vaunting breaks, the world trembles. An epic war between giant-kind and the small folk. Levels 5–15.

synopsis:
For millennia, the Vaunting has governed all of giantkind — an ancestral order set down by Vantorr the First Giant that placed storm giants at the apex and hill giants at the base, with every giant knowing their exact rank and purpose. It was brutal, it was rigid, and it kept the peace. Then it shattered. No one knows why. Some say the giants had grown too complacent to hold it; others believe it broke under a transgression lost to myth. Whatever the reason, the Vaunting is broken, and every giant in Kerreth now scrambles to prove their worth in a world without hierarchy. Hill giants devour entire counties to grow the largest. Stone giants carve prophecies of apocalypse into mountain faces. Frost giants launch longship armadas down the Cormorant Coast. Fire giants enslave thousands to rebuild the Gravenmark, an ancient colossus meant to exterminate dragonkind. And in their cloud castles, the aristocratic cloud giants scheme and betray, each convinced they deserve to sit atop the new order.

Above them all, the storm giants — once the wisest and most noble of their kind — have fallen into disarray. King Vethran, lord of the Skyfast and the one giant who might have held the peace, has vanished. His daughter, Princess Vesarra, holds the throne by a thread, surrounded by advisors she cannot trust and sisters who whisper rebellion. But Vesarra has seen something in the storm-visions that terrifies her more than civil war: a shadow behind the chaos, an ancient intelligence manipulating the giants toward mutual destruction. The ancient blue dragon Vashryn has infiltrated the storm giant court disguised as one of their own, poisoning alliances and engineering Vethran's disappearance. If the dragon's conspiracy succeeds, giantkind will tear itself apart — and the small folk of the Cormorant Coast will be ground to dust beneath their warring feet.

The party enters this cataclysm as unlikely champions. A rune-carved stone falls from a storm-wracked sky, carrying Princess Vesarra's desperate plea for aid — not from giants, who cannot be trusted, but from the small folk who have the most to lose. To answer her call, the party must travel the length and breadth of the Cormorant Coast, confronting giant lords in their own strongholds, forging alliances with those few giants who still seek peace, and unraveling Vashryn's web of lies before the conspiracy plunges the entire continent into a war that will reshape the world. The stakes are measured in mountains toppled, cities crushed, and coastlines redrawn — and the only thing standing between civilization and annihilation is a handful of adventurers brave enough to look a storm giant in the eye.
hook: The storm comes without warning. One moment the sky over Wainscross is clear autumn blue; the next, thunderheads pile up from horizon to horizon in a wall of bruise-purple cloud that moves against the wind. Lightning walks across the farmlands in great stuttering steps, each bolt striking closer, and the cattle bolt for the treeline as the air turns sharp with ozone. The townsfolk barely make it to shelter before the downpour hits — sheets of rain so heavy they bend the signposts and turn the crossroads into a river. Then comes the bolt. A single, blinding lance of white-blue lightning strikes the center of the crossroads with a crack that shakes the foundations of every building in town. When the afterimage fades and the ringing stops, there is something in the smoking crater: a rune-carved stone the size of a dinner plate, still crackling with electricity, humming with a deep resonance that you feel in your teeth. As you approach, the runes flare to life, and a voice — enormous, desperate, unmistakably female — echoes from the stone in a language that somehow translates itself directly into your mind: 'I am Vesarra, daughter of Vethran, Princess of the Skyfast. My father is gone. My people are at war. A serpent coils in our court and I cannot trust my own blood. I beg you — small folk, brave folk — come to me. The world is breaking and you are my last hope.' The stone pulses once more, projects a shimmering map of the Cormorant Coast with a single glowing point far to the north over open ocean, and then goes dark. The storm passes as quickly as it came. The silence it leaves behind is deafening.

setting.name: The Cormorant Coast and the Far Frontier
setting.description: The vast western coast of Kerreth stretches from the sun-drenched farmlands of the south to the ice-locked fjords of the far north — a thousand miles of civilization clinging to a narrow strip between the Wracksea and the untamed wilderness beyond. Great cities dot the coastline: Anchorhold, the City of a Thousand Masts; Cindermoor, rebuilt from volcanic ruin; Gullrest, where pirate lords rule from salt-crusted towers. Between them sprawl farming counties, mining towns, logging camps, and trading posts connected by roads that have never been entirely safe. But now those roads are death traps. Giant footprints crater the King's Road. Boulder-shattered caravans litter every mountain pass. Entire villages have been scooped up and carried away. The land itself bears the scars of the Vaunting's collapse — forests flattened by hill giant stampedes, coastlines reshaped by frost giant raids, mountainsides glowing red where fire giant forges burn day and night. Above it all, cloud castles drift like slow-moving storms, their shadows blotting out the sun for hours as they pass. This is a world where the geography itself has become a battleground, where every elevation — from the deepest valley to the highest peak — is contested by beings who measure their height in tens of feet and their grudges in centuries.
setting.atmosphere: The world feels enormous and terrifyingly fragile. Every horizon holds the silhouette of something that shouldn't exist at that scale — a humanoid figure tall enough to pluck birds from the sky, a fortress carved from a single glacier, a castle floating on a thunderhead. The beauty is breathtaking: frost giant longships cutting through aurora-lit seas, fire giant forges painting the night sky in rivers of orange and gold, stone giant sculptures so vast they reshape the mountains that hold them. But the terror is ever-present. A hill giant raiding party can reduce a thriving town to rubble and bones in a single afternoon. A frost giant warship can freeze a harbor solid. The ground shakes with footsteps that register on the Richter scale. For the small folk — humans, elves, dwarves, halflings — this is what it feels like to be insects in a world of gods. Every giant encounter is a confrontation with scale itself, a reminder that the party is fighting in a conflict between beings who could crush them underfoot without noticing. Courage isn't just an asset here — it's a prerequisite for survival.

regions.name: The Ravaged Lowlands
regions.description: Once the breadbasket of the Cormorant Coast, the rolling farmlands and gentle hills south of Wainscross have become a wasteland of trampled fields, collapsed barns, and scattered refugees. Chief Mavva, a hill giant of staggering size and insatiable appetite, has declared herself queen of the lowlands and launched a campaign of gluttony that defies comprehension. Her hill giant followers raid every farm, granary, and livestock pen within a hundred miles, dragging the spoils back to Cobbleheap — a crude fortress built from stolen timber and piled earth where Mavva gorges herself endlessly, growing larger by the day. She believes that sheer mass will prove her superiority in the broken Vaunting. The human cost is devastating: refugee camps choke every road north, militias are overwhelmed, and starvation stalks the countryside as winter stores vanish down giant gullets. Smoke rises from burning homesteads day and night. The few adventurers who've gone south to confront the problem haven't returned. Amidst the destruction, rumors circulate of a conch shell in Cobbleheap — a magical artifact that could teleport the party directly to the Skyfast and Princess Vesarra's court.

regions.name: The Frozen Reaches
regions.description: North of Gullrest, the world turns white and merciless. Glacial highlands sweep toward the Floe Sea, where frost giant longships — each one large enough to carry a hundred warriors — prowl between cathedral-sized icebergs hunting for the legendary Hoarfast Ring. Jarl Halvarn commands the frost giant fleet from Drifthold, a floating iceberg fortress that drifts through the arctic sea like a frozen mountain with a heartbeat. Halvarn is convinced that the Hoarfast Ring — an artifact of supreme cold magic — will grant him the power to freeze the entire Cormorant Coast and claim dominion over all giantkind. His raiders pillage coastal settlements with brutal efficiency, dragging captives back to serve as thralls in the ice-mines. The land itself is hostile: blizzards that last for weeks, crevasses hidden beneath fresh snow, and temperatures that kill the unprepared in hours. Stone giant caverns honeycomb the mountains nearby, their inhabitants carving apocalyptic murals in the dark and sleepwalking across the surface in a trance-state they call the Dream. The few friendly settlements — Hearthwall, Rimegarth — huddle behind walls and pray for spring.

regions.name: The Cinderworks Depths
regions.description: Deep beneath the volcanic peaks of the Ashfell Mountains, Duke Vharkul's forge-kingdom blazes with hellish industry. The Cinderworks is a fire giant stronghold carved into the heart of a volcano, where rivers of magma serve as both power source and defense. The heat alone kills the unprepared — temperatures soar past anything surface-dwellers can endure without magical protection. Vharkul is perhaps the most dangerous of the giant lords because his ambition has a concrete and terrifying shape: the Gravenmark, a colossus of adamantine and fire that the ancient giants built millennia ago to wage war on dragonkind. Vharkul has found the fragments and is reassembling the construct, using an army of enslaved dwarves, humans, and orcs to work the forges day and night. When completed, the Gravenmark will stand over a hundred feet tall and possess the power to level cities with a single step. Fire giant patrols scour the mountains for more slaves and more adamantine, and the smoke from the Cinderworks' forges can be seen for fifty miles. The approach is treacherous: volcanic vents, lava tubes, salamander nests, and fire giant sentries posted at every chokepoint. But somewhere in the depths, Vharkul keeps a conch shell that could change the course of the war.

regions.name: The Stormreach Above
regions.description: Above the world, where the clouds thicken into something almost solid, the domain of the cloud and storm giants sprawls across the sky. Cloud giant castles drift on enchanted cumulus, each one a palace of marble and mist ruled by an aristocrat convinced of their own superiority. Countess Aravelle is the most prominent — a political mastermind who hoards secrets the way dragons hoard gold, playing every faction against every other while her sky-castle drifts above the chaos in serene detachment. She knows more about Vashryn's conspiracy than she lets on, and her price for sharing will be steep. But it is the Skyfast that dominates the Stormreach — Princess Vesarra's citadel, a fortress of living storm perched on a permanent thunderhead above the trackless northern ocean. Lightning crawls across its walls like ivy. Thunder rolls through its halls like breathing. Here, Vesarra holds court in her missing father's throne, flanked by advisors whose loyalty is uncertain and sisters — Calthea and Doryn — who openly question her right to rule. The storm giant court is a nest of intrigue, and somewhere within it, wearing a giant's face and speaking with a giant's voice, Vashryn the ancient blue dragon watches and waits and smiles.

explorationRules: The Cormorant Coast is vast and the giant war has made every mile dangerous. Overland travel between regions takes 3-7 days depending on terrain and weather, with the party covering roughly 24 miles per day on foot or 30 miles mounted. Each day of travel requires a DC 12 Wisdom (Survival) check to navigate safely; failure triggers a random encounter from the Giant War Encounter table, which scales by region — hill giant foraging parties in the lowlands, frost giant raiding columns in the north, fire giant slave-catchers in the mountains, and cloud giant observation patrols everywhere. The DM rolls 1d6 each morning and evening: on a 1-2, the party encounters evidence of giant activity (massive footprints, demolished structures, fleeing refugees); on a 3, they encounter giants directly. A faction reputation system tracks the party's standing with each giant type — aiding frost giants against fire giants improves standing with Jarl Halvarn but worsens it with Duke Vharkul. Reputation affects whether giants attack on sight, parley, or offer aid. Environmental hazards are constant and region-specific: avalanches and hypothermia in the Frozen Reaches, volcanic gas and lava flows near the Cinderworks, boulder-storms in the lowlands where hill giants hurl rocks for sport, and vertigo-inducing wind shear in the Stormreach Above. Magical conch shells found in each giant lord's stronghold can teleport the party directly to the Skyfast, providing critical shortcuts. The party should be encouraged to forge alliances with friendly NPCs — Lampwright agents, Black Ledger spies, Cities' Concord soldiers, and the rare peaceful giant — who can provide intelligence, safe houses, and alternative routes through contested territory.
